column1: # env_ref_grammar_v1.tsv — the CONTRACT between the two independent
# The grammar is duplicated by necessity — pmcp-package is the workspace-
# excluded leaf crate and neither crate may depend on the other — so this file
# is what keeps the duplication accountable. Both crates assert every row:
# CHANGING A ROW IS A DELIBERATE GRAMMAR CHANGE. Both implementations must move
# in the same commit, or one of the two parity tests fails — which is the whole
# point. A row one side accepts and the other rejects is a config that packs
# cleanly and then fails to resolve at boot (or the reverse), and that is
# exactly the class of bug this table exists to make loud.
#   column 1  the raw config value. The literal token `<EMPTY>` means the
#             empty string (a TSV cannot carry an empty leading field).
#   column 3  what the toolkit's `parse_env_ref` must return:
#                                           to an empty name, which the toolkit
# The two columns differ in SHAPE, not in verdict: `parse_env_ref` answers
# "does this name a variable?" while `is_env_reference` answers "may a package
# defer this key to the environment?". An empty variable name is a reference
# the runtime can act on (by omitting the value) but is NOT something a package
# can ask a target environment to fill, so `${}` and `env:` are Some("") on one
# side and `false` on the other. Encoded here rather than papered over.
